title: The King Walk Checkmate!
transcript: [Music] Take a look at this middle game. Who do you think has the advantage here? Well, interestingly, white not only has the advantage, white has a forced checkmate in seven moves. How's that even possible, you might wonder? Well, the sequence starts with the absolutely beautiful queen takes H7 check. Now, of course, the only move for the black king is to take that queen because the f7 square is covered by the knight. So, well, so what? After the king takes the queen, we have this double check with the knight and the bishop, the king has to come out. And now the other knight can go to G4 like this. And notice how every single square around the king is taken and defended by one of the white pieces. So, black can only go to G5. And after G5, we follow up with H4. Once again, there's only one square available for this black king, the F4 square. So that's where the black king goes. And now there is a follow up with G3. And once again, the only square available is one for the black king, F3. And after F3, here comes bishop E2 check. And you guessed it, there's only one square for the black king, the G2 square. So, we have escorted this black king across the board all the way into our territory. And now it's time for the final hit. We're going to go rook H2 check and bring the black king side by side with the white king. And finally, we can deliver a checkmate by castling long. And finally, we can deliver a checkmate by castling long. What's the craziest commission you have ever found?
